new_defect_discovered_while_verifying.mechanistic_interpretation: v0.5.1 has no sliding-window inference code path at all (that was added in v0.5.2). Bio_ClinicalBERT has a bounded max-sequence-length; without sliding-window chunking, long real pathology reports are truncated at inference time, so entities located after the truncation point are structurally unreachable, not just imprecisely predicted -- a real, mechanistic (not merely statistical) reason for low recall on long reports.
new_defect_discovered_while_verifying.consequence: ClinicalBertModalClient.parse() correctly rejects 100% of tested real reports (0/8, using validate_clinicalbert_contract()) against the currently-live deployment. This is kept as an honest, reproducible FAILING test, not mocked around.

anomaly_now_mathematically_reconciled.anomaly: Two conflicting micro-F1 numbers existed for ClinicalBERT: 0.2534663099 (this receipt, model-card, IN_CORPUS, 296 reports, 2084 sliding windows) vs 0.0809 (a separately-cited fleet-matrix figure).
anomaly_now_mathematically_reconciled.resolution: Hit the live /info endpoint directly this session: test_micro_f1 = 0.08089260808926081 -- an exact match to the fleet-matrix 0.0809 figure. These are NOT two measurements of the same model; they are two DIFFERENT real model versions. 0.0809 (v0.5.1, no sliding window) is what is actually deployed and live-callable today. 0.2535 (v0.5.2-sliding-window, with per-report entity coverage beyond a single 512-token pass) is a newer, real (non-synthetic), better-performing model that exists in the repo/local weights but was never d -- confirmed by the complete absence of its signature fields (model_sha256, metrics_sha256, window_tokens) in the live response.
anomaly_now_mathematically_reconciled.standing_verdict_unchanged: Both 0.2535 and 0.0809 remain far below any usable ship threshold and neither may be headlined as a working parser. The reconciliation explains WHY the two numbers differ; it does not rescue either one.
